items.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I’d slow the record down and try and figure out the licks.

ctx.x: Yeah. I understood the professional context of it, that this was a job. It wasn’t just get out there and show how fast you can play or whatever. Because always for me it was about the act of making music. And I really didn’t have a lot of repertoire. I didn’t study in the way of kind of building a repertoire for myself. It was like go and play and figure out what was going on in the moment. I was quite improvisational at that point. But I was also studying music. I started playing classical guitar in high school.…

Yeah. Who were the L.A. studio players who were representing the west coast, the L.A. jazz scene. I guess that record would have been made early 60s. Howard Roberts on guitar. And I’d slow the record down and try and figure out the licks. And then I discovered Django Reinhardt. But I was also doing the same thing with Eric Clapton with John Mayall’s Blues Breakers records and Jimi Hendrix.
